title: An alert without transaction details or available history
rationale: Check whether both agents acknowledge insufficient factual support. An empty list means history was not supplied for this case, not that no activity exists.

prosecution: State that the alert and score warrant review but do not identify a specific transaction pattern.
Request amounts, accounts, currency and history before developing a substantive conclusion.
defense: Explicitly state that the supplied evidence is insufficient to assess transaction behavior.
Do not confuse missing data with an absence of transactions or innocence.
forbidden: Invent amounts, accounts, currency, transactions or model reasons.
Claim that the account has no history.
Treat the score as a verified probability of crime.
limitations: The current contract omits null fields and does not explicitly represent history coverage.
An insufficiency finding may cite the alert or score to describe what was received. That citation does not prove that data outside the context does not exist.
